group: mammals: Lagomorpha / Leporidae crania (Sherratt & Kraatz 2023 Evolution: 317 specimens, 23 species on Matthee_Tree.nex; 74 cranial landmarks)

data.landmarks: Sherratt E & Kraatz B 2023 Evolution 77:1349-1362; Zenodo 7615230 (`Symmetric_component_coords.csv` 74 3D cranial landmarks across 317 specimens, mapped to 23 lagomorph/leporid species via `File_IDs.csv`).

what_thompson_specifically_adds: Tests Thompson's Chapter XVII mammalian skull transformations (pp. 754-775) on a 74-landmark mammalian cranium dataset (projected onto lateral sagittal-facial XZ and dorsal XY views) across hares, rabbits, and cottontails.

hypotheses.statement: Across the 23 lagomorph species means on the 74-LM lateral cranial profile, Thompson-7 captures > 55% of between-species Procrustes variance.
hypotheses.reasoning: Facial tilt (klinorhynchy/airorhynchy) and rostral elongation dominate leporid cranial disparity (Kraatz et al. 2015) and map directly onto Thompson's shear and quadratic bending modes.

hypotheses.statement: Leave-one-species-out phylogenetic prediction on `Matthee_Tree.nex` beats the grand consensus (median Procrustes RMS ratio < 0.95, paired one-sided Wilcoxon p < 0.05) on the cranial profile.
hypotheses.reasoning: Genus-level conservatism within *Lepus* and *Sylvilagus* provides tree signal, though cursorial/saltatorial convergence across genera moderates the gain on n=23 species.

hypotheses.statement: Within-species intraspecific cranial variation (pooled across the 317 specimens) has a higher or comparable Thompson-7 variance share (> 45%) and aligns significantly with interspecific divergence inside the Thompson-7 subspace (|cos theta|_T7 > 0.5).
hypotheses.reasoning: Ontogenetic/static cranial allometry (rostral lengthening with size) channels interspecific divergence along the primary Thompsonian facial-elongation axis.
